ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited 
Q2 & H1 FY2027 Earnings Conference Call 
October 14, 2026 
 
 
Moderator: Good evening ladies and gentlemen. A very warm welcome to ICICI Lombard 
General Insurance Company Limited's Q2 and H1 FY2027 Earnings Conference Call.  
From the senior management we have with us today Mr. Sanjeev Mantri – MD & CEO of the 
company, Mr. Gopal Balachandran – CFO, Mr. Anand Singhi – Chief Corporate, International, 
Banca, KRG & Government Business, Mr. Girish Nayak – Chief Enterprise AI & Technology,                 
Mr. Sandeep Goradia – Chief Retail Business Strategy & Solutions Team, Mr. Gaurav Arora – 
Chief Commercial Lines & Motor (Underwriting & Claims) and Mr. Girish Sehgal - Chief Health 
UW & Claims, Customer Service. 
Please note that any statements, comments are made in today's call that may look like 
forward-looking statements are based on information presently available to the management 
and do not constitute an indication of any future performance as future involve risks and 
uncertainties which could cause results to differ materially from the current views being 
expressed. 
As a reminder all participant lines will be in the listen only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call please signal an operator by pressing “*” and then “0” 
on your touchtone phone. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Sanjeev Mantri, MD and CEO, ICICI Lombard General 
Insurance Company Limited. Thank you and over to you sir. 
Sanjeev Mantri: Good evening to each one of you. Thank you for joining the earnings 
conference call of ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited for half year ended 
September 30, 2026.  
I would like to commence with an overview of the economic and industry trends followed by 
our company's performance and key initiatives. Our Chief Financial Ofﬁcer, Mr. Gopal 
Balachandran, will then take you through the ﬁnancial performance for the half year ended 
September 30, 2026.  

 
 
3 
 
 
 
The domestic economy continued its growth momentum, with real GDP expanding by 7.8% 
year-on-year in Q1 FY2027. Economic activity remained ﬁrm, aided by private consumption, 
manufacturing growth and investment spending. Supportive monetary and ﬁscal policies 
helped cushion the impact of the ongoing conﬂict in West Asia and broader geopolitical 
tensions on domestic economic activity. 
Looking at speciﬁc industries in the context of our business, the automobile sector, basis data 
from VAHAN, continued to witness strong double-digit growth across key segments during 
H1 FY2027 with total vehicle sales reaching 15.6 mn showing a growth of 21.1%. More 
importantly, the growth of industry across all segments was higher in Q2 FY2027 than in                     
Q1 FY2027, with the overall growth in Q2 FY2027 being 26.9% against Q1 growth of 16.0%.  
September 2026 was a particularly strong month, with total vehicle sales growing by 32.0%. 
This sustained demand provides a healthy base as we enter the key festive months. 
Bank credit growth remained robust at approximately 19.6% in Q2 FY2027, compared with 
17.6% in the preceding quarter. Lending to industry, services and agriculture grew between 
15.0% and 20.0%, including approximately 15.0% growth in credit to large industries. These 
trends indicate broad-based credit demand and supportive ﬁnancing conditions across both 
business investment and household consumption which is always a positive for our sector. 
Talking about regulatory updates, as you would be aware, IRDAI has recently released a 
landmark consultation paper titled “Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution”, which 
seeks to address the evolving needs of the insurance sector, with underlying emphasis on 
transparency, customer trust and distribution efﬁciency. This is expected to result in 
simplifying distribution structures, improving accessibility and enhancing customer 
experience. We believe that the broad objectives outlined in the paper are aligned with the 
long-term vision of ‘Insurance for All’. 
Further, the GST Council in its meeting held on October 08, 2026 has recommended further 
process reforms along with certain measures for trade facilitation and streamlining 
compliances. Within this, an important clarification relates to removal of restrictions on 
availing input tax credit (ITC) on Group - Health and Life Insurance. This recommendation will 
ensure a smoother flow of ITC across the supply chain.  
Let me now dwell upon the industry performance for the period ended September 30, 2026.  
 

 
 
4 
 
 
 
The General Insurance Industry continued to demonstrate steady GDPI growth of 8.9% in                    
H1 FY2027, supported by 10.9% in Q1 FY2027 and 7.0% in Q2 FY2027. However, the GDPI 
growth excluding Crop and Mass Health segments was 12.6% in H1 FY2027.  
 
Speaking of specific segments within the industry: 
 
• 
The Commercial lines segment witnessed an improvement in growth trends during                         
Q2 FY2027 as compared to the preceding quarter. Most of the key segments, namely 
Engineering, Marine, Liability and Miscellaneous i.e. the segments sans Fire insurance, 
collectively reported a healthy growth of 15.9% for Q2 FY2027. While the Fire segment 
continued to witness a de-growth of 26.6% for H1 FY2027, the pace of decline moderated 
to 24.4% in Q2 FY2027 as against 27.8% in Q1 FY2027 with September at a de-growth of 
only 13.6%. These trends indicate a gradual improvement in the operating environment for 
Commercial lines, which augurs well for the segment in the coming quarters. 
  
• 
As highlighted earlier, the Motor segment continued to record healthy growth. Notably, EV 
penetration across passenger vehicles and two wheelers surged 1.5 times, rising from 6.4% 
to 9.7%, with a combined 1.3 million vehicles sold during H1 FY2027. 
 
The industry registered a growth of 13.1% in Motor insurance, for H1 FY2027 vis-a-vis                  
H1 FY2026.  
 
Moving into the festive season, we expect the Motor sales to continue surpassing previous 
trends. However, growth may appear to be moderated on account of a higher base.  
 
• 
Health continues to be the fastest-growing segment for the General Insurance industry. 
The segment reported a robust growth of 21.0% for H1 FY2027. Within Health Insurance, 
the Group Health line of business grew by 15.3%, while Retail Health recorded a healthy 
growth of 32.0% during the same period. 
 
As mentioned earlier, the recent GST Council recommendation to allow Input Tax Credit on 
employer-sponsored Group Health Insurance is a welcome development. Improved 
affordability could encourage wider employee health coverage among SMEs and larger 
corporates, supporting the segment's growth. 
 
 
 

 
 
5 
 
 
 
Speaking on the Underwriting Performance of the Industry: 
 
The underwriting performance of the General Insurance industry continued to remain under 
pressure, with the overall Combined Ratio (CoR) deteriorating to 116.8% in Q1 FY2027 from 
115.0% in Q1 FY2026. 
 
Within this, the industry's Combined Ratio for the Motor segment deteriorated signiﬁcantly to 
131.4% in Q1 FY2027 from 125.0% in Q1 FY2026, driven by an increase in both LR (loss ratio) 
and commission ratio, reﬂecting continued pressure on underwriting proﬁtability. 
 
Against this backdrop, ICICI Lombard's Motor Combined Ratio moved only marginally to 
108.3% in Q1 FY2027 from 107.6% in Q1 FY2026, primarily attributable to the impact of the 
Supreme Court judgement (Shishupal), as discussed during our previous earnings call.  
 
Consequently, the delta in Combined Ratio of Motor between the industry and the Company 
widened signiﬁcantly to 23.1% points in Q1 FY2027 from 17.4% points in Q1 FY2026. This 
widening differential reinforces the strength of our underwriting discipline, pricing capabilities 
and claims management practices, enabling us to sustain our leadership position while 
consistently delivering superior outcomes relative to the industry. 
 
I will now proceed to present our Company’s performance across key business segments for 
H1 FY2027. 
 
The Company reported a growth of 5.4% in Gross Direct Premium Income (GDPI) for                         
H1 FY2027, compared to the industry growth of 8.9%. Further, the GDPI growth of the 
company excluding Crop and Mass health segment was 13.9% for Q2 FY2027 as compared 
to industry growth of 13.2% on similar lines. 
   
• Within our Commercial lines segment, Q2 FY2027 witnessed a signiﬁcant improvement 
over the preceding quarter. Excluding Fire, our Commercial lines portfolio registered a 
healthy growth of 20.0% in Q2 FY2027 and 13.2% for H1 FY2027, with broad-based 
traction across Lines of Business (LoBs). Within Fire, the pace of decline moderated 
signiﬁcantly, with de-growth reducing to 21.2% in Q2 FY2027 from 32.1% in Q1 FY2027. 
Pertinently, the de-growth for the month of September 2026 moderated further to just 6.0%, 
reﬂecting a sequential improvement through the quarter. Our market share in the Fire Line 
of Business for the period ended H1 FY2027 stood at 12.2%.  
 

 
 
6 
 
 
 
We have gained market share in Q2 FY2027 vis-à-vis Q2 FY2026 in Fire from 11.4% to 
11.9%, in Marine cargo from 17.1% to 19.0%, in Engineering from 15.8% to 16.4% and in 
Liability from 16.1% to 16.6%. We maintained our leadership position in the Marine Cargo 
and Engineering Lines of Business as at H1 FY2027. 
  
• 
In the Motor segment, we recorded a healthy growth of 13.0% for H1 FY2027, broadly in 
line with the industry growth of 13.1% for H1 FY2027, thereby maintaining our market 
leadership position with a market share of 10.3% for H1 FY2027. We remain focused on 
strengthening our granular distribution across OEMs, dealerships and diversiﬁed retail 
channels, thereby expanding our market reach while maintaining a balanced portfolio mix. 
 
Our portfolio mix for Private Car, Two-wheeler and Commercial Vehicle stood at 49.8%, 
28.1% and 22.1% respectively, for H1 FY2027. 
 
As indicated during our Q1 FY2027 earnings call, the Company made incremental 
provisions towards its Motor Third Party reserves, following the Supreme Court judgement 
in the Shishupal case, in line with our prudent and conservative reserving philosophy. Given 
that the judgement was delivered towards the end of the quarter, the Company had 
recognized the impact on the entire portfolio for Q1 FY2027, resulting in an incremental 
reserving requirement. 
 
During Q2 FY2027, we have calibrated our business operations to factor in the implications 
of the judgement, and the same has now been fully integrated into our regular course of 
business. 
 
Looking ahead, we are well positioned to enhance our market positioning given the robust 
volume growth as reﬂected in VAHAN data, increased retention rate and signiﬁcant 
difference in our Combined Ratio versus that of the Industry in the Motor insurance 
Segment.  
 
• In the Health segment, we recorded a healthy growth of 26.8% for H1 FY2027, as against 
the industry growth of 21.0% for H1 FY2027. 
 
Our Retail Health business continued to demonstrate strong growth of 66.4% for                         
H1 FY2027, signiﬁcantly outpacing the industry growth of 32.0% for H1 FY2027. 
Consequently, our market share improved to 4.7% for H1 FY2027 from 3.7% for the 
corresponding period last year. Pertinently, we exited September 2026 with our market 

 
 
7 
 
 
 
share in Retail Health reaching 5.0% for the ﬁrst time, reﬂecting the sustained strength of 
our Retail Health franchise. 
 
The Group Health segment recorded a growth of 15.4% for H1 FY2027, with our market 
share remaining stable at 8.8% for H1 FY2027, in line with the corresponding period last 
year. 
 
On August 03, 2026, ICICI Lombard marked its Silver Jubilee, celebrating 25 years of 
operations. As we step into the next phase of our journey, we remain committed to driving 
innovation, strengthening our customer promise and creating sustainable long-term value. 
We extend our heartfelt gratitude to all stakeholders for their trust and support, which 
continue to inspire our progress. 
 
To commemorate this signiﬁcant milestone, ICICI Lombard unveiled 25 innovative solutions 
across multiple lines of business including offerings such as Complete Home Protect, Paw 
Care, Motor Service Assure and Power Booster Plus, amongst others. Notably, these 
comprised 5 industry-ﬁrst and 7 industry-leading solutions.  
 
Further, the Company organised its Digital Day in the last week of September 2026, where 
we showcased how technology is closely integrated with our business operations and is 
helping drive tangible outcomes across key areas, including product development, 
underwriting, claims management and customer servicing. I would like to thank all of you who 
took the time to participate in the event. 
 
On the same day, we also launched our latest Health insurance offering, Vibe, for our Gen 
customers, designed to provide a comprehensive wellness solution that goes beyond 
traditional Health insurance protection. The product reﬂects our continued innovation in 
making Health insurance more relevant and accessible to the younger generation. 
 
AI and Agentic AI are enhancing claims accuracy, accelerating genuine claims and 
strengthening fraud-risk assessment with human oversight. Precision rates on leakage/fraud 
related triggers have improved from 45% to 60% through usage of GenAI. Adoption of our 
digital journeys for customer service continues to grow, with 73% of the total customer 
interactions being handled through digital Do-It-Yourself (DIY) journeys as against 39% last 
year. 
 

 
 
8 
 
 
 
In Health underwriting, our industry ﬁrst Whatsapp based Gen AI bot helps customers 
complete their underwriting through a conversational interface enabling a more 
comprehensive risk assessment and faster turnaround times. This journey now is used in over 
40% of our agency new business daily.  
 
The initiatives I have outlined reﬂect our continued focus on leveraging technology and 
innovation to strengthen our business capabilities and drive sustainable, proﬁtable growth. 
As articulated during our recent Digital Day, one of our key strategic priorities is to scale up 
digital sourcing with a deﬁned roadmap to elevate its contribution from the current 6.0% to 
15% thereby reinforcing our commitment to innovation and future ready distribution.   
 
I will now request Gopal to take you through the ﬁnancial numbers for H1 FY2027. 
 
Gopal Balachandran:  Thanks Sanjeev and Good Evening to each one of you.  
 
Before I proceed with giving a brief overview of the ﬁnancial performance of the recently 
concluded quarter and half year, would like to share herewith some aspects w.r.t to our key 
initiatives, as an organization. 
 
o Our IL TakeCare app, a one-stop solution for insurance and wellness needs, achieved 
23.3 million downloads as at September 30, 2026, reﬂecting growing digital adoption.  
o The total number of health and travel claims serviced through the IL Take Care App 
witnessed an uptick by 25.6% and reached 3,78,583 claims for H1 FY2027.  
o Our Preferred Partner Network (PPN) serviced 75.9% of our non-OEM claims for                     
Q2 FY2027 vis-à-vis 75.1% for Q2 FY2026. 
o In the Health segment, 99.2% of our total claims were paid within 30 days for                         
H1 FY2027. 
o 93.0% of the customers surveyed as part of our IL Sahayak initiative, have rated their 
experience as exemplary i.e. have given us a score of > 4.5/5. 
 
Now moving on the ﬁnancial performance, we have uploaded the ‘Results Presentation’ on 
the exchanges. You can access it as we walk you through the performance numbers. 
 
All numbers mentioned below are on n basis, unless stated otherwise. Please refer our 
investor presentation (slide nos. 14 to 17) which has got details of outcomes on both n & 1 by 
n for further details.  
 

 
 
9 
 
 
 
Our Combined ratio was 104.5% in Q2 FY2027 as against 103.9% in Q2 FY2026. Excluding 
the impact of CAT losses of ₹ 1.18 billion in Q2 FY2027 and ₹ 0.73 billion in Q2 FY2026, the 
Combined ratio was 102.7% and 102.6% respectively. 
 
• 
Combined Ratio was 105.2% for H1 FY2027 as against 103.0% for H1 FY2026. Excluding 
the impact of CAT losses of ₹ 1.18 billion in H1 FY2027 and ₹ 0.73 billion in H1 FY2026, 
the Combined ratio was 104.2% and 102.3% respectively. 
Our investment assets during the quarter rose to ₹ 643.32 billion as at September 30, 2026, 
from ₹ 605.79 billion as at June 30, 2026. Our investment leverage (net of borrowings) was 
3.58x as at September 30, 2026, as against 3.59x as at June 30, 2026.  
On a quarterly basis, investment income was at ₹ 15.54 billion in Q2 FY2027 as against                         
₹ 12.49 billion in Q2 FY2026. Investment income was at ₹ 27.28 billion in H1 FY2027 as 
against ₹ 25.38 billion in H1 FY2026. 
Capital gains stood at ₹ 4.53 billion in Q2 FY2027 as compared to ₹ 2.36 billion in Q2 FY2026. 
Our capital gains stood at ₹ 6.37 billion in H1 FY2027 as compared to ₹ 6.16 billion in                         
H1 FY2026. 
Our Proﬁt before tax (PBT), grew by 27.8% at ₹ 13.59 billion in Q2 FY2027 as against ₹ 10.63 
billion in Q2 FY2026 whereas PBT de-grew by 5.8% and stood at ₹ 19.21 billion in H1 FY2027 
as against ₹ 20.39 billion in H1 FY2026.    
Consequently, PAT grew by 27.5% and stood at  ₹ 10.31 billion for Q2 FY2027 from ₹ 8.09 
billion in Q2 FY2026. Our Proﬁt after tax (PAT), de-grew by 5.8% and stood at ₹ 14.54 billion 
in H1 FY2027 as against ₹ 15.43 billion in H1 FY2026.    
The RoAE for Q2 FY2027 was 23.7% as against 21.3% in Q2 FY2026. Return on Average 
Equity i.e., RoAE was 16.8% in H1 FY2027 as against 20.7% in H1 FY2026. 
Solvency ratio was at 2.74x as at September 30, 2026, as against 2.68x as at June 30, 2026, 
continued to be higher than the minimum regulatory requirement of 1.50x. Solvency Ratio 
was at 2.62x as at March 31, 2026.  
The Board of Directors of the company has declared interim dividend of ₹ 7.00 per share for 
H1 FY2027 as against ₹ 6.50 per share for H1 FY2026. 
 

 
 
10 
 
 
 
As I conclude, I would like to reafﬁrm that we continue to stay focused on driving proﬁtable 
growth and sustainable value creation while protecting the interest of our stakeholders and 
customers at all times.  
 
With this, we will be happy to take questions from all of you.  
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. We will now begin with the question and answer 
session. Our ﬁrst question comes from the line of Nischint Chawathe with 
Kotak. Please go ahead. 
Nischint Chawathe: 
Just two questions. One was, I was looking at the change in Motor TP 
claims ratio on a sequential basis is almost 2,000 basis points. So, I was 
just curious how to read this. Have you provided for the recent Supreme 
Court verdict this time around and what could be the ratio ex of that? The 
second question is obviously on the distribution reforms and how do you 
see that affecting your business? 
Gopal Balachandran:    So Nischint thanks for that. This was obviously an expected one. I think 
we have always maintained that at an aggregate level, third-party is 
always the line of business that exhibits a long tail liability of claim 
development. 
                                        Hence, to that extent, the time at which we provide for ultimate loss 
reserves and let us say the development of claims paying out obviously 
takes time. Hence, to that extent, we have always maintained to kind of 
look at outcomes particularly for Motor third-party over long cycles, 
ideally on a year-to-date basis or ideally over longer annual cycles. 
Having said that, I think if you look at our particular loss development 
patterns over years, particularly in the third-party book, I think we have 
generally followed a principle of prudence at the time when we have 
underwritten the risk and the portfolio is always exhibited consistently 
over long periods, a small amount of reserve releases. 
Hence, to that extent, a particular quarter will also get inﬂuenced by 
some of this development of losses getting actualized. Hence, to that 
extent, the loss ratios are what they are in terms of its ultimate depiction. 
Having said that, I think if all of you would recollect, I think we have been 

 
 
11 
 
 
 
kind of proactive even in Quarter 1 when the judgment had come in to 
call out the need for the industry to get impacted consequent to this 
judgment. 
On that basis, the available information that we had at that point of time, 
I think we had considered for a reserving requirement of ₹1.65 billion in 
Q1. Having said that, we did at the same time in the call, did speak about 
to make sure that as an organization, we would want to kind of take this 
going forward as a business-as-usual element. Hence, to that extent, 
what we have been able to achieve is on the extent of the reserving, we 
do not anticipate any need for any further requirement of provision for 
reserves. 
To that extent, of course, we will continue to monitor in terms of what the 
development of court judgments are because as I said, the book takes 
time to kind of play out. But at this point of time, in line with what we had 
said, honestly, it is now a part of our business as usual and genuinely, we 
do not believe the need for us to separately call out any speciﬁc 
additional charge consequent to the Supreme Court judgment. So, that 
is where we are on the change in the Motor third-party loss ratio. 
                                      On the distribution reforms, and maybe I think I will request.... 
 Sanjeev Mantri: 
So, clearly, as we also said to our investors, it is a landmark change, truly 
a recalibration in terms of how insurance will get distributed probably 
from next year onwards and whatever the regulator has put across is a 
reboot in many ways. We have seen across industry in the past that

that is where the penetration equation that we want will call out for us

100% binding and we look forward to this evolving over time and coming

It is, if you look over quarters, will be a big plus for the industry in every

12 
 
 
 
Nischint Chawathe: 
Sure. And given the fact that commissions have, I mean, are potentially 
coming off signiﬁcantly, do you see the risk of third-party tariffs getting 
revised downwards? 
Sanjeev Mantri: 
I mean, look, every call, I think Nischint, you are right, every call we have 
had this discussion where the current economics used to make us believe 
that we would seek a hike in third-party. How does it get viewed out? 
How does the paper get ﬁnalized?

with it. But at the same time, we have seen judgments changing the

addressed. But all I can say is you got a point and we are as much 
processing it at this point of time as anybody else. And it may change the 
economics. My answer is yes, how, only time will tell.

We have our next question coming from the line of Supratim Dutta with

So, we see that on the Motor side, there has been a mix shift with the 
share of two wheelers going up this quarter. Just wanted to understand 
what role has that played in the Motor TP loss ratio, if any. So, that would 
be my ﬁrst question. The second would be on IFRS accounting, I do 
understand that the commission ratio being higher is again a function of 
this two-wheeler mix going up. If you could, given you would have the 
ﬁrst quarter ﬁnancials on IFRS with the regulator, if you could give us 
some color on 1/N and N, we know what the economics look like. But if 
you transition to IFRS, how would these numbers change? If you could 
give us some color there, that would be really appreciated.

quarter, like you give, that would also be very helpful. Thank you.

 Thanks, Supratim. I think I will go in the reverse order. I will start with the 
loss ratios on Group Health.

numbers in the current Quarter 2 for Group Health is 97.9% and retail

actually closer to 100, almost about 99.9%. So, relative to that, on a

Corporate Health loss numbers. So, in that sense, that is a good sign 
and genuinely we believe, I think even so far as the way forward is 
concerned, we should continue to see efﬁciencies coming on the 
Corporate Health side. So, that is on the Group Health, I mean the Health 
loss ratios breakdown. On IFRS, I think honestly Supratim, I think we 
have always maintained, we will deﬁnitely come back to all of you and 
we will explain in terms of what the impact is on account of, let us say, 
the change from IGAAP to IFRS. 
                                      Yes, you are right, we had to kind of do the regulatory ﬁlings of Q1 by 
September 30, which is what we have done. And having said that, I think 
we will obviously come back and maybe at a separate point of time, take 
all of you through in terms of what do we see, how do we see the impact 
of the change from Indian GAAP to IFRS play out. Having said that, I 
think we will continue to reiterate that one should keep looking at one 
form of reporting on a consistent basis for any form of comparisons. 
Relative comparisons honestly will not necessarily lead you to any 
meaningful outcomes. So, we will come back. On the Motor third-party

loss ratio, I think just to again kind of reiterate, we have always 
maintained the outcome of the combined ratio of Motor in speciﬁc. 
                                      You are right, it gets inﬂuenced by what we write as a mix, what we kind 
of incur as a cost of acquisition, etc., etc. And that is the reason why, and
